description: If “Output prefix” under C/C++ Build -> Settings -> Build artifact points outside of the configuration directory, then when the project is cleaned, the artifact is not deleted.\\n\\nSteps to reproduce:\\n\\n1. Create C project based on Hello World ANSI C Example\\n2. Set “Output prefix” in C/C++ Build -> Settings -> Build artifact to   \\n    ..\\\\n3. Compile the project --> <project>.exe is created under the project directory\\n4. Clean the project --> <project>.exe is not deleted from project directory

description: Steps to reproduce:\\n\\n1. Create C project based on Hello World ANSI C Example\\n2. Add a source file that compiles\\n3. Build the project\\n4. Exclude the source file from the project\\n5. Build the project again --> note that all the files are recompiled when only linker should be run\\n6. Include the source file back to the project\\n7. Build the project --> note that all the files are recompiled when only linker should be run\\n\\nIn steps 5,7 the whole project is recompiled when only linker should be run.
title: Exclude/Include of the source file from the project causes recompilation of all files

description: Build ID: I20070601-1539 + CDT 4.0 RC3\\n\\nSteps To Reproduce:\\n0. ensure that workspace auto-refresh is disabled\\n1. create an HelloWorld project (gcc)\\n2. add some command line flags producing some extra files (eg: -dl -dA -dn)\\n3. compile with external make builder: all generated files (*.c.<int>.<ext>) are immediately visible to the user in the output directory\\n4. switch to the internal builder, clean and rebuild project: only the .o/.exe files are visible. The internal builder probably assumes that it knows all output files, but then you need to manually refresh the output directory to see the other files generated by the compiler.\\n\\nThis is somehow related to bug 163652 which requests a way to disable the automatic refresh on build (here we want to force the refresh). Maybe the internal builder should at least explicitly perform a refresh in order to behave the same way as the external make builder ...
title: Internal builder does not refresh whole output directory

description: After a new project is created, CDT creates the Debug/Release directory and builds it ok. Perhaps CDT should detect that directory is gone, much like it detects if a file is modified, and issue a clean build.

description: This bug is related to bug #178716 (https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=178716)\\n\\nIt would be nice to be able to customize the built-in includes CDT automatically creates. description: Build ID: I20070621-1340\\n\\nSteps To Reproduce:\\n1. Create a new MinGW C++ project on Windows with more than one source file.\\n2. Right-click the project in the project view.\\n3. Choose Properties.\\n4. In the left if the window that comes up, choose C/C++ Build.\\n5. Click the Behavior tab.\\n6. Check \\"Use Parallel Build\\".\\n7. Click \\"Use Parallel Jobs:\\".\\n8. Fill in 2, or the number of CPU's/cores you have.\\n9. Expand C/C++ Build.\\n10. Click Settings.\\n11. Click the Build Steps tab.\\n12. In pre-build events, fill the Command field with some program you know of, like C:\\\\windows\\\\notepad.exe.\\n13. Click OK.\\n14. Ensure Build Automatically is turned off in the Project menu.\\n15. Run the project, letting it build.\\n16. Once the build completes, modify ONE of the source files and again press run.\\n17. Note that it sometimes rebuilds both files as if you had done a clean, and that notepad does not start as part of the pre-build event.\\n\\nMore information:\\nNOTE: You -may- need a multi-cpu/core system to reproduce this bug - I don't know for sure.\\n\\nYou may also try turning off Parallel Build to see that everything works fine without it on.

description: Bug 348700 fixed a severe regression late in the game. This bug is for following-up with more investigation and probably a cleaner solution.\\n\\nParticularly, in VT100TerminalControl#disconnectTerminal(),\\n\\n- The Connector should likely be disconnected BEFORE terminating the reader job\\n  (otherwise with high data volume, the connector can write into a pipe that's\\n  no longer being read from, or even closed)\\n\\n- The Reader should have a more clean method of terminating fast (other than\\n  interrupting the entire Thread, which may cause InterruptedException at a\\n  time where it's not desired, for instance while processing characters - \\n  see bug 333613 comment 2)\\n\\n- Revisit whether it makes sense to keep the PipedInputStream alive and \\n  open for the entire lifetime of the VT100TerminalControl, even when \\n  different connections read/write to it.\\n\\nTest cases for these improvement include\\n- disconnect / reconnect terminals\\n   - both from the Terminal (pressing button)\\n   - and from the remote side (pull network cable, connection-lost, EOF)\\n- Terminate Eclipse with multiple terminals open.
title: [terminal] Revisit closing Terminal Reader Thread

People who search help for \\"terminal\\", \\"command prompt\\", \\"console\\",\\n      \\"git bash\\" or \\"shell\\" find the Terminals View\\n   2. People who press F1 in the Termninals View or dialog find basic docs\\n      about interesting keyboard shortcuts and workflows.\\n\\nWe don't want to document each and every icon, but there should be \\"Terminals View\\" documentation in the Eclipse Help. Similar to what the TM Legacy Terminal View had provided. Doc content could mostly be taken from the Marketplace Listing at \\n   https://marketplace.eclipse.org/content/tcf-terminals\\n\\nContext help IDs should be provided for the Terminals View, the Local Terminals Preference Page, the Terminal Widget Preference Page, and probably the Terminal Launch Dialog (eg mention where Passwords are saved).
title: [TERMINALS] Provide help documentation for terminals

And as a result, programs that work on a normal terminal don't work on Eclipse.\\n\\nOSX should configure \\"--login\\" by default if $SHELL is bash at least.
